category_title: Students who actively distance themselves from non-reading family environments
scenario_title: Struggling with assigned whole-class texts in traditional English courses
minimal_context: The student is participating in 30 minutes of independent reading using the assigned whole-class text.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Demetrius, it is time for our 30 minutes of independent reading. Please take out the assigned class novel and begin reading the next chapter.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Okay, I have it out. I will try to read it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just focus on the pages we need to cover today.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I'm trying, but it's hard for me to read this specific book. We are not really a family that reads that much, except for me, so I'm used to just reading by myself when I find something I like.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Keep trying, we all have to read this same book for the course.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I know that if you read you do better in school or English, and I really want to get a good grade. But I wasn't really raised to be read to, and I just can't get through this assigned text no matter how politely I sit here.

task.content: Reading one whole-class text for instruction

context.environment: English courses and reading-intensive elective course
context.materials: One whole-class text, self-selected texts, reading logs
context.social_setting: Whole-class instruction, book groups, conferencing quietly with peers or the teacher

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When participating in required English courses that primarily focused on one whole-class text for instruction
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Consistently received poor grades in his English courses despite being a polite, friendly student
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Understood family norms as socially constructed and actively distanced himself from his non-reading family
related_quotes: We are not really a family that reads that much, except for me.
It was not an impairment but in a way it was . . . I wasn’t really raised to be read to

behavior_patterns.condition: Describing the process of learning to read and seeking academic assistance
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Solicited the extra help he needed to become a good reader
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Assumed responsibility for his successful reading growth; ownership over his reading suggests that being a successful reader was something he wanted for himself
related_quotes: So I was self-taught at first, and then I started getting extra help, and just started loving to read.
If I had kids, I would definitely read to them because it is proven that if you read to a kid or you make them read, then overall, they do better in school or English.
